children: The U.S. fired 70 or more of its high-end air defense interceptors to counter Iran's missile attack on Jordan last week, officials familiar with the matter told
, amid concerns over dwindling weapon stockpiles.

U.S. forces fired 60 to 70 Patriot interceptors and more than a dozen THAAD interceptors to counter Iran's attack, which consisted of about 20 ballistic missiles. Iran managed to hit aircraft at the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan.
The Pentagon has been pushing for defense contractors to ramp up production amid concerns over arms stockpiles.

While President Trump said the U.S. has "large numbers" of Patriots, THAAD systems, Tomahawks, and other Standard Missile systems in stock, a Pentagon official flagged "strategic inventory shortfalls" and "industrial base bottlenecks for munitions resupply" in a report this week.
produced a record 620 Patriot interceptors in 2025 and is targeting to manufacture about 2,000 a year.
The U.S. expended about 1,700 Patriot air defense interceptors and over 200 THAAD anti-missile interceptors in the war by mid-July, the
reported. U.S. Navy ships fired another 150 Standard Missile interceptors to down Iranian missiles and drones.

"The main opportunity cost of the conflict thus far has been the large expenditure of missile defense interceptors, which will leave the U.S. with a reduced inventory of interceptors for several years," the Congressional Budget Office noted.
Interceptors are expensive, ranging from ~$4M for Patriot and SM-6 interceptors to $12M for THAAD interceptors and $28M for the most sophisticated SM-3 interceptors.

The CBO estimated that the cost of replacing the interceptors expended through Aug. 1 could reach $13.1B. It said rebuilding the Pentagon's inventory of interceptors would probably take at least five years, even if production increased.

title: U.S. said to burn through interceptor supplies to thwart Iran attacks
